Senses.PreferredTarget: full capacity for action comes into view
Senses.Explanation: Full capacity for action comes into view rather than remaining merely available or described. The expression occurs 447 times in 170 allowlisted texts and often continues with the statement that established rules are not retained. Dazhu Huihai directly equates the appearing of great function with the unequalled body of the teaching. A reviewed unnamed monk asks Changqing Da'an what happens when great function appears without retaining rules; Changqing answers, “If you can use it, just use it.” Fengxue Yanzhao tells the assembly that at the encounter great function must appear and that they must not constrain themselves to small details. Yunmen Wenyan states the stock line; a second reviewed unnamed monk immediately asks what the appearing of great function is, and Yunmen raises his staff and calls out that old man Shakyamuni has come. Yuanwu Keqin pairs the stock line with using a blade of grass as a sixteen-foot golden body and the golden body as a blade of grass. Dahui Zonggao reports that students of sayings apply the phrase to Guizong's killing a snake and Nanquan's killing a cat, then explicitly rejects that account. Zen makes a phrase about capacity becoming present into a public question, an assembly demand, and a case-commentary formula; the different answers and Dahui's rejection prevent any one action from becoming its hidden definition.
Senses.Note: The direct question asking what the appearing of great function is occurs 22 times in 19 texts, and the exact at-the-encounter collocation occurs twice in two texts. Named speakers and reviewed unnamed questioners supply many different replies and actions; the entry reports representative deployment shapes and Dahui Zonggao's explicit rejection without assigning a single hidden force to them.

Occurrences.Kwic: 大用現前即是無等等法身。又問。性中有惡否。師曰。此中善亦不立。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Record of the Transmission of the Lamp Published in the Jingde Era (景德傳燈錄), Dazhu Huihai directly equates great function appearing with the unequalled body of the teaching in his extended sayings.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：大用現前，不存軌則時如何？

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The finite marker 'a monk asked' directly governs the complete question; Changqing Da'an's answer begins only afterward.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Joint Essentials of the Lamps (聯燈會要), Changqing Da'an section: a monk whom all six attribution rungs leave unnamed asks what happens when great function appears without retaining rules; Changqing Da'an answers only after the stored question.

Occurrences.Kwic: 示眾云：大凡參學眼目，直須臨機大用現前，勿自拘於小節。設使言前薦得，猶是滯殻迷封；句下精通，未免觸途狂見。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Joint Essentials of the Lamps (聯燈會要), the governing Fengxue Yanzhao section identifies this as Fengxue Yanzhao's address to the assembly.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師有時云：大用現前，不存軌則。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Joint Essentials of the Lamps (聯燈會要), Yunmen Wenyan section: Yunmen Wenyan states that great function appears and established rules are not retained.

Occurrences.Kwic: 時有僧便問：如何是大用現前？師拈起拄杖高聲云：釋迦老子來也。

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The finite marker 'a monk then asked' governs the direct question; Yunmen Wenyan responds by raising his staff and calling out.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Joint Essentials of the Lamps (聯燈會要), Yunmen Wenyan section: a monk whom all six attribution rungs leave unnamed asks what the appearing of great function is; Yunmen Wenyan answers by raising his staff and calling out that old man Shakyamuni has come.

Occurrences.Kwic: 歸宗斬蛇。南泉斬猫兒。學語之流。多謂之當機妙用。亦謂之大用現前不存軌則。殊不知。總不是這般道理。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Sayings Record of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄), Dahui Zonggao's instruction to Layman Li explicitly reports and rejects this labeling of the Guizong and Nanquan cases.

Occurrences.Kwic: 所以道。大用現前。不存軌則。有時將一莖草。作丈六金身用。有時將丈六金身。作一莖草用。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu's Blue Cliff Record (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄), Yuanwu Keqin deploys the stock phrase in his prose comment.
